one_liner: Ranks every number by the fitted curve's value at the next draw, using a Chebyshev minimax polynomial of degree 2 over the last 52 draws, smoothed fitted to its record of being drawn or not.

short_explanation: E_3 looks at each number on its own, as a record of 1 (drawn) or 0 (not drawn) over recent draws. It first smooths the 0/1 record of the last 52 draws with a running average over up to 9 draws, then fits the polynomial of degree 2 whose worst single error is as small as possible (Chebyshev minimax, found exactly by the exchange method). It then ranks the numbers by the fitted curve's value at the next draw: its top pick is the highest-ranked numbers and its inverse pick the lowest-ranked, with exact ties settled by the project tie rule (TIE_SHA256_V1). The scores are curve values, not chances, so no probabilities are published. A curve fitted to a short, noisy record is least reliable exactly at its end, which is where this method looks; that is what the experiment measures. It uses only which numbers were drawn, not their order or the dates, and needs 52 earlier draws. If the draws are fair, it is not expected to beat chance.
